% A guard: it checks cases that the fix of the files read with the
% primitive \input must not break.
% Files of the document that name themselves like glossary.4ht with
% \ProvidesFile{glossary.tex}, read with the primitive \input inside a
% file read with \input{}, and in the body. As in the PDF, each file's
% text is in the page.
% The body's \ProvidesFile comes after tex4ht reads the .4ht files, so
% that line checks only that the name raises no error there.
\documentclass{article}
\input{test-priminput/chapter}
\begin{document}
Nested: \primnested\par
Chapter: \primchapter\par
\input test-priminput/body
\end{document}
